# fluss-go v0.1.0-beta.6

This prerelease stabilizes transport and lookup shutdown behavior and expands
remote-storage integration for Apache Fluss 0.9.1 clients.

## Highlights

- Preserves the reader-side connection failure when a peer closes immediately
  after receiving a request instead of replacing it with a redundant
  write-deadline cleanup error.
- Prevents point and prefix lookup calls racing with `LookupClient.Close` from
  being stranded after scheduler shutdown.
- Adds an optional Alibaba Cloud OSS remote-file adapter based on the official
  OSS SDK for Go v2.
- Adds an HDFS remote-file adapter boundary for application-owned clients with
  exact range and metadata validation, cancellation-driven close, and cloned
  filesystem-token cleanup.
- Reuses protocol-neutral object URI, byte-range, and content-range validation
  across the S3 and OSS adapters.
- Clarifies that deprecated `Descriptor` methods shown for `fmsg` are
  compatibility shims generated by `protoc-gen-go`; the message types and
  protocol API are not deprecated.

## Upgrade notes

- Importing `adapters/oss` adds the official Alibaba Cloud OSS SDK for Go v2.
  Applications continue to own region, endpoint, credentials, retry policy,
  and SDK client lifecycle.
- `adapters/hdfs` intentionally does not select an HDFS protocol dependency.
  Applications provide an `hdfs.OpenFunc` backed by a maintained internal or
  vendor-supported client that owns Kerberos and delegation-token handling.
- Existing S3, local-file, and custom `RemoteFileReader` implementations remain
  compatible.
- The OSS and mounted-HDFS service tests are opt-in because they require
  external credentials or a configured HDFS mount. Their required variables
  are documented in each adapter manual.

See the [full changelog](../../CHANGELOG.md), the
[remote-storage guide](../../docs/remote-storage.md), the
[OSS adapter manual](../../adapters/oss/README.md), and the
[HDFS adapter manual](../../adapters/hdfs/README.md).

This is a pre-v1 release. Pin the version and review the changelog before
upgrading.
